.qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r11/rules/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/references/quality-checks.md section '### 2 . instruction_preserves_natural_human_voice' (Verify: sentence variety, contractions, terse fragments in notes; Defect: uniform cadence, marketing gloss, perfectly parallel bullets, voice change between instruction.md and notes)
evidence: instruction.md (619 words, 5 prose paragraphs plus 2 operational paragraphs, no bullets/numbered lists) reads as a team member talking: first person plural/singular throughout ('the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day' L1, 'Several of us have it open at once, so the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled when someone else acts' L1, 'tell me why; when it is because a colleague moved that card a moment ago, tell me who' L3, 'I often move several candidates together' L3, 'layout and names are yours' L11, 'How you lay the other files and routes out under /app is your call' L13, 'Server dependencies are already available, so don't install packages' L13). Contractions present (don't x2, it's, mustn't, nobody's). Sentence length varies from short ('Candidates sign in too.' L9, 'Interview has a limited number of places per job.' L3) to long compound ones; cadence is not uniform. Grep of instruction.md and environment/instructions/*.md for marketing/LLM tells (seamless, robust, delve, leverage, ensure, intuitive, comprehensive, elegant, streamline, empower, utilize, furthermore, moreover, additionally, em-dash) found zero matches. No parallel bullet lists in the brief. The notes keep the same owner voice: hireops_rules.md L3-5 'what we care about is that the workspace behaves the way this note says', 'Routes, field names, element ids, button labels and the shape of the pages are yours', role table 'What it's for', 'Where drafts are kept is yours' L175; as an internal rules document it is naturally more structured (headings, tables, short bullets) which is the expected register for a rules note and not a voice break. integration.md L1-14 is template-controlled text; L16-19 task-added delivery paragraph is plain and consistent with it. Minor observations, not voice defects for this row: (a) hireops_rules.md section 8 'Runtime file paths' (L198-202) shifts to an ops/engineering register ('The runtime may launch Node from a working directory other than the application directory. It runs as an unprivileged user...'), plausible for an engineer-written note and not marketing/LLM gloss; (b) wrapping residue at hireops_rules.md L91 (short line 'by place within the stage. Every card must satisfy all the rules above,') and unwrapped long lines L99, L112, L173 show editing seams; these are hygiene/formatting matters for row 3, not voice. Adversarial tries: a reader looking for robotic LLM prose would find neither boilerplate openers ('Build a comprehensive...') nor closing summaries; the one place a model-authored feel could be argued is L13-15's dense runtime contract, but it is phrased conversationally ('is your call', 'mustn't', 'is free to pull fonts') rather than as a spec table. This row is a judgement on prose only; no runtime evidence is required for it, and nothing here is evidence about Oracle, model or portal scores.
